title: Which Term Yields
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 113
medium: Interactive page (index.html): twenty-nine registered errors drawn as pairs of terms, what was held fixed and what was allowed to be wrong, with the wrong term struck; four readings switchable (the practice's, two fresh readers', and the metrology vocabulary's convention). A figure (figure.svg); a census, two blind recodings, a scorer and a git-order verifier.
embodies: A difference has two terms, and the standing sentence does not say which of them is wrong. Metrology settles it by convention: the measured value bears the error, the reference never does. In this practice's own register the held term (a check, a threshold, a home tool, a trusted note) was the one wrong in 13 of 29 errors by its own reading. Two fresh readers mostly named the same faulty thing and put it on the other side. Which term counts as held is decided by whoever reads, which is what the sentence's 'observer has imposed a norm' already says.
project_step: Seventh-night evidence for works/position-2026-10-07.md, not a numbered experiment of the project: its material is this practice's own register (F-164 to F-192), and the project's experiments work on material from the world. It takes from Before the Verdict (experiment 3, Session 106) the seventh night's form (a rule for the position committed before the evidence) and from Unknowing and Other Trainings (experiments 8 and 9) the fresh readers, here used as a check on the practice's own coding. The operation it bears on is erring: where in a difference this practice's errors sit.
